notes: Values in mg/l unless stated. Standards is the shared heading above the four destination columns.
Rows 4, 13 and 29 have one printed cell spanning all four standard columns, expanded here. Radioactive materials is a group heading and No 28 spans its alpha and beta rows.

Row 34 overrides destination headings: first two value columns are onto land, (J) 1,000 and (K) 10,000; last two are into water, (J) 1,000 and (K) 10,000. These must not be interpreted under the ordinary destination headings.
Colour and odour / Public Sewers is a blank printed cell, retained as an empty string.

A. These standards shall be applicable only if such sewer leads to a secondary treatment including biological treatment system; otherwise the discharge into sewers shall be treated as discharge into inland surface waters.
B. All efforts should be made to remove colour & unpleasant odour as far as practicable.
D. For cooling water effluent 10% above total suspended matter of influent.
E. Shall pass 850 micron IS Sieve
H. Shall not exceed 5°C above the receiving water temperature
I. 90 % survival of fish after 96 hours in 100 % effluent
Source: The Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986 in http://cpcb.nic.in/GeneralStandards.pdf

Following paragraph on page 308: historical BOD not exceeding 20 mg/L and SS not exceeding 30 mg/L; this manual recommends, for treated sewage discharged into surface waters used as a source of drinking water, BOD not exceeding 10 mg/L, SS not exceeding 10 mg/L, Total Nitrogen as N not exceeding 10 mg/L, Dissolved Phosphorous as P not exceeding 2 mg/L, Faecal coliforms not exceeding 230 MPN / 100 ml. More details in Table 5-20.
